recipes.name: Extra-Yummy Fluffy Pancakes
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon vegetable oil, or as needed

steps.text: Whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt in a large bowl. Whisk in milk, beaten egg, 3 tablespoons vegetable oil, and vanilla until only a few lumps remain. Let batter stand for 5 full minutes for extra fluffiness.

Heat a griddle over medium heat and brush with 1 teaspoon vegetable oil. When oil shimmers, slowly pour about 1/4 cup batter onto the hot griddle and cook until bubbles form and the edges are dry, about 2 minutes. Flip and cook until browned on the other side, about 2 minutes more. Repeat with remaining batter.

raw_recipe.headline: Extra-Yummy Fluffy Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: These vanilla pancakes are light, fluffy, and made with egg, cinnamon, and milk for a tasty breakfast dish that tastes delicious with berry syrup

review.reviewBody: Great recipe for "Extra-Yummy" Pancakes with a nice touch of cinnamon! I used only two tsp. of cinnamon vs. a full Tbsp. and added a full tsp. of vanilla for good measure. Also, letting the batter rest for a few minutes while the frying pan heats up makes for really fluffy pancakes. These were perfect topped with butter and REAL maple syrup! Also equally awesome with sauteed apples over top...

I don't like cinnamon all that much, so I added just a teaspoon of cinnamon for just a hint of that cinnamony flavour with a teaspoon of vanilla. I have a bag of self raising flour I want to get rid of, so I just used it instead of plain flour with baking powder. I had to add a bit extra milk (maybe a few teaspoons?) before I thought the consistency of batter good enough. Despite the many changes, the pancakes turned out absolutely divine! It was my first time making pancakes, and I will definitely make them again. Pancakes w/ maple syrup for dinner ftw!

Although they weren't what I would consider "fluffy," these pancakes were delicious. This matches the recipe I typically use with the exception of the addition of the vegetable oil in the batter and I use a generous sprinkle of cinnamon rather than a tablespoon. I also add a full teaspoon of vanilla. The trick to getting the pancakes a nice, golden color seems to be a very hot pan a minimal amount of oil for each pancake. I also suggest making sure there are plenty of bubbles in the exposed batter before you flip the pancakes. The pancakes are very thin (think McDonald's hotcakes), but they are tasty and just as delicious when reheated!

Quick, easy and the kids ate 3-4 pancakes each. No joke! I was a little concerned about put 1 tablespoon of cinnamon into the batter but it seemed to work. I did add a full teaspoon of vanilla & aside from that followed the recipe exactly. The key is to let the batter rest as long as possible. Delicious with chopped apples on the side & some whip cream. YUM!

These pancakes were amazing! I cut the cinnamon down to 1 teaspoon, (as I am not a fan of it) and letting the batter sit for 5-10 minutes make the perfect combination for a perfect pancake. Delicious!
These were the best pancakes ever :D I made them with half the amount of cinnamon and out dark chocolate real maple syrup and bananas on them they were amazing i’m sure to use this again

I didn't have regular milk on hand so I used sour cream. I've read on different sites that sour cream can be a substitute for buttermilk recipes. I still mixed the sour cream with vinegar. These pancakes came out so moist and fluffy.

Mine did not come out very fluffy, but they were still tasty. We only added about 1 1/2 tsp cinnamon, and even that seemed like a bit much, but it was a nice change from plain pancakes. I probably won't make these exactly the same next time, but I think I will cross this and the other Fluffy Pancakes recipe we use (use buttermilk or soured milk, melted butter instead of oil) next time. I do love that this recipe included vanilla! Surprisingly, many pancake recipes do not, so we always add it as our "secret ingredient" :) All in all, I do recommend trying this one - just use your discretion as far as the amount of cinnamon is concerned!
I followed the recipe with the addition of bananas to half of the batter and blueberries to the other. Everything came out great and plan on making these again.

Huge hit in my house, everyone loved them! I followed the exact recipe, no tweaks. These babies fluffed up like nobody’s business. I made a double batch and we had for breakfast and lunch. We like to put peanut butter on our pancakes and the cinnamon with the peanut butter, for me, wasn’t my cup of tea. Still really good but next time I’ll leave it out and maybe just do a little more vanilla.

I have made them twice, and both times the were a hit. They are light and fluffy, a touch sweet. They brown nicely. I leave out the cinnamon all together. The second time I made them, I accidentally forgot the vanilla. They were still good, but it definitely makes a difference; don't forget the vanilla.

I tried to follow the recipe but there was too much cinnamon and the pancake mix was runny. I tried to compensate by adding more flour and sugar to thicken the mix up. I will not be making this recipe again

the recipe was good and i got pancakes as a result but they were missing something because they didn't hold together easily and didnt turn out as circles or got cut while flipping them, they also weren't fluffy they were thin
Its tastes good, isn't too sweet, and very soft if you cover with butter after cooking. Good Recipe.

The pancakes were very bland. I had to add a little bit more sugar and a little less Cinnamon the oil was way too much I only put 2 tbsp and still it was too much. My sister rated it a 1/10 and I rate it a gracious 4/10. Would not try again!

Too much cinnamon, pancakes came out looking dark brown because of the cinnamon. they even tasted like nothing. This is a terrible recipe! The batter was so dark too! and the pancakes smelled like cinnamon but didn’t taste like anything. where was the flavor?
These were ok. Not fluffy, and the batter was runny so I knew they wouldn't be fluffy.. I even put less milk in because I saw the batter was not thick enough.
